decisions.reason: Define-XML ADADAS.CHG states only AVAL - BASE, and its literal probe (adadas-documented-rules.yaml lines 184-187) gives 0 on the 3800 records where the reference leaves CHG missing, which are the ABLFL = 'Y' baseline records with a score. ADRG pages 17, 45 and 48 concern the LOCF analysis and the imputation differences and state no baseline suppression that would reproduce the reference.

ADRG page 11 describes placing collected visits into analysis visits by their dates; its counterpart is the obs AVISIT windowing (adadas_v1.yaml lines 438-446), not the constant visit of an added record. ADRG page 47's R-generated example shows exactly this for an imputed record: the Week 16 LOCF record carries the Week 8 record's VISIT and date, as locf8, locf16 and locf24 do.

CL.AVISITN is shared by IT.ADADAS.AVISITN and IT.ADLBC.AVISITN (native define-adam.xml lines 1190 and 1579), so its other entries serve ADLBC's visits. The obs mapping (adadas_v1.yaml lines 452-459) gives the codelist's own codes for Baseline, Week 8, Week 16 and Week 24, the only AVISIT values the specification derives, so it states the same numeric code for AVISIT on this dataset.

Each LOCF template takes ADT and ADY from the same donor record (adadas_v1.yaml lines 537-538 and 548-549), whose ADY obs computed by study_day from that ADT and the subject's TRTSDT. The copied ADY therefore equals the Define-XML ADADAS.ADY formula applied to the record's own ADT; it is the same arithmetic by another route.

Define-XML ADADAS.BASE adds (QS.VISITNUM=3) to QS.QSBLFL=Y, while the BASE aggregate (adadas_v1.yaml lines 391-401) filters only ABLFL = 'Y' and no layer conditions on VISITNUM. Every ADAS-Cog QSBLFL=Y record in the staged QS is at VISITNUM 3, so the values agree and this is a divergence rather than a conflict.

Define-XML ADADAS.AVISIT delegates windowing to Section 8.2 of the SAP, which is not among Pilot 3's section files and whose applicability is pending_review in spec/source/manifest.json, and ADRG page 11 says only that visits are windowed by date. No retained text gives the study-day cut points 1, 84 and 140, their closure, or the otherwise branch to Week 24 (adadas_v1.yaml lines 438-446).

Define-XML ADADAS.DTYPE only labels imputed ACTOT records LOCF, and ADRG pages 45-47 give the number of imputed records and one example of an added Week 16 record. No retained text states the general condition in locf8 (and locf16, locf24) for adding a record: one per subject when the target visit has no ANL01FL ACTOT record and an earlier one exists.

ADRG page 11 states that ADADAS holds the ADAS-Cog questionnaire items, one record per subject per parameter per VISIT, Define-XML ADADAS.PARAMCD limits the parameters to the CL.PARAMCD_ADQSADAS codes ACITM01-ACITM14 and ACTOT, and ADADAS.AVAL reads QS.QSSTRESN where QSTESTCD=PARAMCD. Together they state this QS record selection, and native define-adam.xml line 1248 names QS.QSTESTCD as PARAMCD's predecessor.

Define-XML ADADAS.AVISIT delegates windowing to Section 8.2 of the SAP, which is not among Pilot 3's section files and whose applicability is pending_review in spec/source/manifest.json, and ADRG page 11 states only that visits are windowed by date. Neither gives window boundaries or the visit of an added LOCF record, so no literal probe can be stated.

Define-XML ADADAS.ADY and ADADAS.ANL01FL do not say which record an imputed record's ADY comes from, and ADRG page 47 shows only one R-generated Week 16 record carrying the flagged Week 8 record's day rather than the later unflagged one's. No retained text states the general restriction to ANL01FL = 'Y' ACTOT donors at or before the target visit that adadas_v2.yaml lines 71-72 apply.

Define-XML CL.DTYPE's 'Last Observation Carried Forward' gives only the direction of the carry, and ADRG page 47 illustrates one carried record. No retained text states the donor ranking by AVISITN, then ADY, then QSSEQ, all descending with missing values last (adadas_v1.yaml lines 102-112).

Define-XML ADADAS.ADT states only 'SAS date from QS.QSDTC', and the day-01 imputation in ADRG page 8 section 3.4 is stated for ADAE ASTDT, not ADADAS ADT. No retained text states imputing a missing QSDTC day as the first of the month; every ADAS-Cog QSDTC in the staged QS is a complete date, so the clause does not change values.

Define-XML ADADAS.ADT names only the QS.QSDTC conversion, ADADAS.DTYPE only labels imputed ACTOT records, and ADRG page 47 illustrates one added Week 16 record. The condition _HIT IS NULL AND _SRC_QSSEQ IS NOT NULL under which a record carrying a donor's date is added (adadas_v1.yaml line 529, repeated at lines 563 and 597) has no documentary counterpart.

Define-XML CL.DTYPE's 'Last Observation Carried Forward' gives only the direction of the carry, and ADRG page 47 illustrates one carried date. No retained text states the DONOR16 ranking by AVISITN, then ADY, then QSSEQ, all descending with missing values last (adadas_v1.yaml lines 127-137).

The generic Define-XML ADADAS.AVAL method covers the item parameters, but native define-adam.xml binds ACTOT to MT.ADADAS.AVAL.ACTOT (lines 98-100 and 4425-4428, workbook Methods row 6), which leaves the missing-item adjustment to SAP section 14.2, whose applicability to Pilot 3 is pending_review. With that adjustment unstated the documented ACTOT rule is incomplete, so AVAL cannot be probed across its full scope whatever the section export holds.

Define-XML ADADAS.CHG and workbook Methods row 10 state only AVAL - BASE, and ADRG pages 17 and 45-48 add no condition on baseline records. The guard ABLFL <> 'Y' (adadas_v1.yaml line 407) is therefore unstated, although the reference leaves CHG missing on baseline records as the guard does.

Define-XML ADADAS.PCHG and workbook Methods row 12 state only 100* (CHG/BASE), and no ADRG page adds a baseline-record or zero-baseline condition. The guard ABLFL <> 'Y' AND BASE <> 0 (adadas_v1.yaml line 414) is therefore unstated.

Define-XML ADADAS.PCHG states 100* (CHG/BASE) without saying what PCHG is when BASE is 0, and neither the ADRG nor workbook Methods row 12 supplies that policy. The literal expression is undefined on zero-baseline records, so it cannot be stated as a probe.

Define-XML ADADAS.ANL01FL chooses the visit closest to the target date but gives no rule for two equally close visits, and the ADRG page 46-47 example has no such tie. The second sort key _DIFF (adadas_v1.yaml lines 483-484), which prefers the later visit, is therefore unstated.

Define-XML ADADAS.ANL01FL ranks by closeness to the target date and does not say how a record without a distance is ranked. Placing missing AWTDIFF last (adadas_v1.yaml lines 481-482) has no counterpart in the retained documents.

Define-XML ADADAS.ANL01FL selects among the visits that fall into the same visit window, with no condition on the score, and ADRG page 11 gives the dataset one record per subject per parameter per VISIT, so ranking every collected record of a subject, parameter and AVISIT states that rule. Added LOCF records never compete, since locf8, locf16 and locf24 add one only where the visit has no flagged ACTOT record, and ADRG page 47 shows such a record flagged Y.

Define-XML ADADAS.ANL01FL gives nearest-to-target selection but no tie rule, and the target day itself is delegated by ADADAS.AWTARGET to the SAP, which is not among Pilot 3's section files and whose applicability is pending_review in spec/source/manifest.json. ADRG pages 46-47 illustrate one subject's flags without completing those choices, so a literal probe cannot be stated.

Define-XML ADADAS.DTYPE only labels imputed ACTOT records LOCF, and ADRG pages 45-47 give the number of imputed records and one example of an added Week 16 record. No retained text states the condition in locf8 (and locf16, locf24) under which an imputed record is added: one per subject when the target visit has no ANL01FL ACTOT record and an earlier one exists.

Define-XML ADADAS.DTYPE needs a predicate for an imputed ACTOT record, and ADRG pages 45-48 distinguish collected from imputed records and illustrate one added Week 16 record without stating which visits must exist or when a record is added. An independent probe would have to borrow the specification's LOCF templates or the reference DTYPE, so the documented rule is incomplete.

No claim cites it; it is the record rule that the obs row (each record keeps QS.QSSTRESN, DTYPE missing, adadas_v2.yaml lines 783-787) and the locf8, locf16 and locf24 templates implement.
